correctness.rationale: For rho_{m,k}=Box^{m+k}p -> Box^m p, frame validity is exactly the Boolean relation inclusion R^m subset R^{m+k}, witnessed conversely by a valuation true on all (m+k)-successors. For every n-world frame with m>=n and lcm(1,...,n)|k, any m-walk repeats a vertex and insertion of k/ell copies of a closed segment extends its length by k. In serial frames, at m=n-1 a simple spanning walk can be extended to a terminal-based closed cycle of length <=n. An r-cycle with r∤k and directed dead-end or terminal-loop paths furnish exact obstructions. Consequently b_K=min(m+1,d(k)) and b_KD=min(m+2,d(k)), including n=1 and all m,k>=1. Independent enumeration through three worlds corroborated both quantified criteria but is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp minimum size of a frame countermodel, including the exact serial one-world difference, was not covered by the inspected nearby sources. Knudstorp proves finite-model property for logics axiomatized by reductions, not least falsifying-frame cardinality for one axiom. Boolean-matrix eventual equality is logically distinct from optimal one-sided inclusion R^m subset R^{m+k}; standard cycle-pumping is known, so older automata/Boolean-matrix formulations could overlap.
residual_risks: Older Boolean-matrix path-length inclusion or unary automata pumping results may already imply the sharp cutoffs; full 1999 Boolean-matrix manuscript and all historical variants were not exhaustively inspected.

value.rationale: A natural modal reduction family has a fully determined finite countermodel cutoff for arbitrary m,k, with exact serial/unrestricted separation and deterministic sharp witnesses. This is a meaningful finite test boundary rather than a mere special numeric calculation.
